THOUGHT: The patient is a 31-year-old woman with 4 months of mostly watery diarrhea, lower abdominal cramping that is relieved by defecation, urgency, mucus discharge, and a sensation of incomplete evacuation — features that fit a diarrhea-predominant functional bowel disorder. The temporal clue that someone at a recent camping trip became ill supports a post-infectious trigger. Important alarm features for organic disease are absent: no fever, no weight loss, no nocturnal symptoms, no overt GI bleeding, hemoglobin is normal, ESR is normal, and routine stool exam is unremarkable. Mild leukocytosis (11,000/mm3) is nonspecific and low-grade. Alternative diagnoses considered include inflammatory bowel disease (less likely given normal inflammatory markers, no systemic symptoms, and benign exam), chronic infectious causes such as Giardia (possible but stool testing was normal and there is no weight loss or steatorrhea), microscopic colitis (can present with chronic watery diarrhea and normal basic labs but more common in older patients and often requires colonoscopy/biopsy to diagnose), and celiac disease (screening would be reasonable if symptoms persist). Overall the clinical pattern — chronic diarrhea with abdominal pain relieved by defecation, urgency, mucus, onset after an episode of presumed gastroenteritis, and normal basic testing — most strongly supports post-infectious irritable bowel syndrome / IBS-D. Further evaluation (stool PCR/O&P, fecal calprotectin, celiac serology, or colonoscopy) would be warranted only if symptoms worsen, red flags develop, or initial empiric management fails.

DIAGNOSIS: Post‑infectious irritable bowel syndrome (diarrhea‑predominant IBS, IBS‑D)
